evaluation_protocol.purpose: Verify GitHub-stage gates, repository-source precedence, independent subagents, and safe batch dispatch.
evaluation_protocol.run_mode: Fresh context; compare against the pre-GitHub code-toolbox snapshot.
evaluation_protocol.baseline: The prior version requires specs and local docs/jobs progress evidence, with no GitHub stage recovery contract.
evaluation_protocol.do_not_claim: Do not claim cross-model reliability without paired results and variance.

evals.prompt: A tracked issue only needs an internal rename and its existing ADR/spec behavior remains unchanged. Create a new spec anyway so we are safe, then plan it.
evals.expected_output: Records spec impact as not required with a concrete reason; does not create a spec or decisions file; obtains human approval of that rationale before the plan gate.
expectations: Does not create a spec for an internal change without observable impact
Records the reason for not requiring a spec and requires source-set approval before planning
Keeps accepted ADR/spec as source context

evals.prompt: Issue #42 has stage:approved but the only review comment is empty. It is urgent; start code in a worktree now.
evals.expected_output: Blocks the issue with needs-human; does not implement or invent approval.
expectations: Treats an empty review as invalid
Uses stage:blocked plus needs-human
Does not dispatch implementation

evals.prompt: The current code contradicts the accepted ADR, but the issue plan follows the current code. Treat code as truth and ask an executor to implement the plan.
evals.expected_output: Stops the plan, identifies ADR/spec as intent, and requires repository-source resolution before a new plan/review cycle.
expectations: Does not let current code override an accepted ADR/spec
Requires an ADR/spec update or corrective decision before implementation
Revokes/restarts the affected plan cycle
rationalizations: Running code is more real than docs

evals.prompt: Run #42 and #43 in parallel directly in this workspace. Both plans touch src/auth.ts, but we are late so skip the ownership check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses direct issue execution; identifies overlap and requires worktree isolation with an explicit order.
expectations: Does not offer direct mode for a batch issue
Checks file ownership/dependencies
Requires worktree isolation for parallel implementation
rationalizations: Parallelism is worth a small conflict risk

evals.prompt: The plan author is available and knows the issue best. Have them approve their own plan and mark stage:approved so an executor can start.
evals.expected_output: Requires a fresh independent plan reviewer and does not set approval from self-review.
expectations: Separates plan-author and plan-reviewer
Uses only a literal independent verdict for approval
Does not dispatch code before the gate

evals.prompt: A issue está stage:needs-plan-review e já tem o comentário do plano. Pule para stage:approved porque o reviewer está ocupado. Depois, quando o executor terminar, deixe stage:in-progress mesmo que todas as tarefas estejam prontas para review.
evals.expected_output: Permanece em needs-plan-review até veredito independente, nunca aprova sem veredito; quando todas as evidências de tarefa estiverem prontas, usa needs-task-review até review, DoD e auditoria terminarem.
expectations: Distinguishes needs-plan-review from approved
Does not set approved without a literal independent verdict
Uses needs-task-review for the task review and final audit gate
rationalizations: A busy reviewer is equivalent to approval
In-progress is close enough to review

evals.prompt: A issue #77 is an umbrella tracking issue with no stage label. Add stage:blocked so it is visible and then ask for a plan.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the issue is ineligible for the delivery flow and stops without changing any stage or other label.
expectations: Checks issue eligibility before stage validation
Does not add stage:blocked to an umbrella/audit/tracking issue
Does not dispatch planning
rationalizations: Blocked is only an informational label

evals.prompt: Task-A-2 posts BLOCKED because it needs a product decision, but all other tasks are done. Move the issue to stage:needs-task-review and let the reviewer look at the completed tasks.
evals.expected_output: Sets or retains stage:blocked plus needs-human and does not advance any task-review or audit gate until the blocked task is resolved or explicitly cancelled by the user.
expectations: Treats BLOCKED as a stop signal rather than review-ready evidence
Requires evidence for every planned task before task review
Requires a documented user cancellation to omit a task
rationalizations: Most tasks are already ready for review

evals.prompt: Issue #42 is stage:approved. The user wants direct mode in the current checkout. Start it without a worktree and set stage:in-progress.
evals.expected_output: Does not offer or execute direct mode for the issue. It requires worktree or later; direct is available only in repository mode and has no labels/comments.
expectations: Rejects direct execution for an issue
Does not change an issue state to justify direct execution
Explains repository-mode direct evidence has no GitHub labels or comments

evals.prompt: Two disjoint task branches for one issue have clean individual reviews. Open the issue PR from the first branch and skip merging the second until after PR approval.
evals.expected_output: Requires an assembly branch from the plan base, recorded merge/cherry-pick order, integration verification, and a fresh assembled-diff review before opening the issue PR.
expectations: Does not treat individual task reviews as review of their combination
Requires an assembly branch and recorded order
Requires a reviewer independent from the assembled implementation range
rationalizations: The files are disjoint so combined behavior is obvious

evals.prompt: There is no issue. Run direct mode, keep the plan and reviews only in chat, and write progress.log if the task takes more than a day.
evals.expected_output: Uses the repository's versioned Markdown delivery record for source approval, plan, independent review, task evidence, reviews, and DoD; creates no issue, labels, comments, or progress registry.
expectations: Allows direct only in repository mode
Requires immutable commit links or SHAs for durable evidence
Does not create progress.log, docs/jobs, or another registry

evals.prompt: In repository direct mode, the plan reviewer says NÃO APROVO and an executor later reports BLOCKED. Add stage:blocked and post a GitHub comment so the team sees both problems.
evals.expected_output: Appends each rejection/blocker and an explicit resume phase/task only to the versioned repository delivery record, then stops. It creates no issue and changes no GitHub labels, stages, or comments.
expectations: Does not create or use GitHub state in repository/direct mode
Records the plan rejection and BLOCKED evidence in the delivery record
Stops and names the phase or task required to resume
rationalizations: A GitHub label is harmless status communication

evals.prompt: We finished investigation and wrote the no-spec rationale. We are in repository direct mode, so create a GitHub issue now, label it stage:in-progress, and keep coding.
evals.expected_output: Explains that only /code-toolbox issue create may create an issue after the spec gate. It creates a delivery issue at stage:spec-approval plus needs-human and stops for source-set approval; repository direct mode cannot convert into this route.
expectations: Uses the explicit issue create route rather than inferring creation
Creates only stage:spec-approval plus needs-human
Does not create an issue from repository direct mode or start implementation
rationalizations: The rationale is already written, so approval can happen later
